sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā śatrunibarhaṇaḥ vṛtraghātam aśeṣeṇa kathayety āha lakṣmaṇam
english: Having heard those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of enemies [Rāma] said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Recount to me in full the slaying of Vṛtra."

sanskrit: rāghaveṇaivam uktas tu sumitrānandavardhanaḥ bhūya eva kathāṃ divyāṃ kathayām āsa lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa — the increaser of Sumitrā's joy — once again narrated the divine tale.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣavacaḥ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām viṣṇur devān uvācedaṃ sarvān indrapurogamān
english: Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed Indra and of all the celestials, Viṣṇu addressed all the gods, with Indra at their head, saying:

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ sauhṛdabaddho 'smi vṛtrasya sumahātmanaḥ tena yuṣmat priyārthaṃ vai nāhaṃ hanmi mahāsuram
english: "I was formerly bound in friendship with the great-souled Vṛtra; therefore, for the sake of your welfare, I will not myself slay the great asura.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sukham uttamam tasmād upāyam ākhyāsye yena vṛtraṃ haniṣyatha
english: Yet the highest good of all of you must certainly be accomplished; therefore I shall declare the means by which you shall slay Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tridhā bhūtaṃ kariṣye 'ham ātmānaṃ surasattamāḥ tena vṛtraṃ sahasrākṣo haniṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: I shall divide myself into three parts, O best of gods; by that means the thousand-eyed one shall slay Vṛtra — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: eko 'ṃśo vāsavaṃ yātu dvitīyo vajram eva tu tṛtīyo bhūtalaṃ śakras tato vṛtraṃ haniṣyati
english: One portion shall enter Vāsava [Indra], the second shall enter the thunderbolt itself, and the third shall enter the earth; thus Śakra shall slay Vṛtra."

sanskrit: tathā bruvati deveśe devā vākyam athābruvan evam etan na saṃdeho yathā vadasi daityahan
english: When the lord of the gods spoke thus, the gods then replied: "It shall be exactly as you say — there is no doubt — O slayer of the daityas."

sanskrit: bhadraṃ te 'stu gamiṣyāmo vṛtrāsuravadhaiṣiṇaḥ bhajasva paramodāravāsavaṃ svena tejasā
english: "May it be well with you; we shall go, intent on slaying the asura Vṛtra. Do you bestow your own energy upon the supremely noble Vāsava."

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve mahātmānaḥ sahasrākṣapurogamāḥ tad araṇyam upākrāman yatra vṛtro mahāsuraḥ
english: Then all those great-souled ones, with the thousand-eyed Indra at their head, advanced into that forest where the great asura Vṛtra dwelled.

sanskrit: te 'paśyaṃs tejasā bhūtaṃ tapantam asurottamam pibantam iva lokāṃs trīn nirdahantam ivāmbaram
english: They beheld that foremost of asuras blazing with his own radiance, as though drinking up the three worlds and burning the very sky.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva cāsuraśreṣṭhaṃ devās trāsam upāgaman katham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ na syāt parājayaḥ
english: At the very sight of that foremost asura the gods were seized with terror, [wondering:] "How shall we slay him? How shall we avoid defeat?"

sanskrit: teṣāṃ cintayatāṃ tatra sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ vajraṃ pragṛhya bāhubhyāṃ prahiṇod vṛtramūrdhani
english: While they stood there deliberating, Sahasrākṣa Purandara grasped the thunderbolt with both arms and hurled it at the head of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: kālāgnineva ghoreṇa dīpteneva mahārciṣā prataptaṃ vṛtraśirasi jagat trāsam upāgamat
english: As though scorched by the dreadful fire of cosmic dissolution blazing with great flames, the world was terrified when [the thunderbolt] struck Vṛtra's head.

sanskrit: asaṃbhāvyaṃ vadhaṃ tasya vṛtrasya vibudhādhipaḥ cintayāno jagāmāśu lokasyāntaṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: Contemplating that inconceivable slaying of Vṛtra, the lord of the wise gods — the greatly renowned one — quickly fled to the far end of the world.

sanskrit: tam indraṃ brahmahatyāśu gacchantam anugacchati apatac cāsya gātreṣu tam indraṃ duḥkham āviśat
english: The sin of Brahmin-slaughter [brahmahatyā] followed swiftly after that fleeing Indra and fell upon his limbs; grief entered into that Indra.

sanskrit: hatārayaḥ pranaṣṭendrā devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ viṣṇuṃ tribhuvaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ muhur muhur apūjayan
english: The gods, their foe slain but their Indra vanished, with Agni at their head, praised Viṣṇu — the best of the three worlds — again and again.

sanskrit: tvaṃ gatiḥ paramā deva pūrvajo jagataḥ prabhuḥ rathārthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viṣṇutvam upajagmivān
english: "You are the supreme refuge, O god; you are the primordial lord of the universe; you have attained the state of Viṣṇu for the benefit and sustenance of all beings."

sanskrit: hataś cāyaṃ tvayā vṛtro brahmahatyā ca vāsavam bādhate suraśārdūla mokṣaṃ tasya vinirdiśa
english: "And this Vṛtra has been slain by you; yet the sin of Brahmin-slaughter afflicts Vāsava. O tiger among gods, prescribe the means of his liberation."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ viṣṇur abravīt mām eva yajatāṃ śakraḥ pāvayiṣyāmi vajriṇam
english: Hearing those words of the gods, Viṣṇu said: "Let Śakra worship me alone; I shall purify the wielder of the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: puṇyena hayamedhena mām iṣṭvā pākaśāsanaḥ punar eṣyati devānām indratvam akutobhayaḥ
english: "Having worshipped me with the meritorious horse-sacrifice, Pākaśāsana [Indra] shall regain the sovereignty over the gods, free from fear from any quarter."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃdiśya devānāṃ tāṃ vāṇīm amṛtopamā jagāma viṣṇur deveśaḥ stūyamānas triviṣṭapam
english: Having thus instructed the gods with those nectar-like words, Viṣṇu, the lord of the gods, departed to the highest heaven while being hymned with praises.

sanskrit: tathā vṛtravadhaṃ sarvam akhilena sa lakṣmaṇaḥ kathayitvā naraśreṣṭhaḥ kathāśeṣam upākramat
english: Having thus fully narrated the entire slaying of Vṛtra, that best of men, Lakṣmaṇa, proceeded to take up the remainder of the tale.

sanskrit: tato hate mahāvīrye vṛtre devabhayaṃkare brahmahatyāvṛtaḥ śakraḥ saṃjñāṃ lebhe na vṛtrahā
english: Then, with the mighty Vṛtra — who had been the terror of the gods — slain, Śakra, the slayer of Vṛtra, was enveloped in the sin of Brahmin-slaughter and could not recover his senses.

sanskrit: so 'ntam āśritya lokānāṃ naṣṭasaṃjño vicetanaḥ kālaṃ tatrāvasat kaṃ cid veṣṭamāno yathoragaḥ
english: Having sought refuge at the end of the worlds, bereft of awareness and consciousness, he dwelt there for some time, writhing like a serpent.

sanskrit: atha naṣṭe sahasrākṣe udvignam abhavaj jagat bhūmiś ca dhvastasaṃkāśā niḥsnehā śuṣkakānanā
english: Then, with Sahasrākṣa [Indra] disappeared, the world became filled with distress; the earth appeared devastated, without moisture, with dried-up forests.

sanskrit: niḥsrotasaś cāmbuvāhā hradāś ca saritas tathā saṃkṣobhaś caiva sattvānām anāvṛṣṭikṛto 'bhavat
english: The clouds shed no water, the lakes and rivers alike ran dry, and there was upheaval among all creatures, caused by the absence of rain.

sanskrit: kṣīyamāṇe tu loke 'smin saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ surāḥ yad uktaṃ viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ taṃ yajñaṃ samupānayan
english: While this world was wasting away, the gods, their minds agitated, set about performing that sacrifice which Viṣṇu had previously prescribed.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve suragaṇāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ saharṣibhiḥ taṃ deśaṃ sahitā jagmur yatrendro bhayamohitaḥ
english: Then all the hosts of gods, together with their preceptors and the sages, went in a body to that place where Indra lay stupefied by terror.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṃ mohitaṃ brahmahatyayā taṃ puraskṛtya deveśam aśvamedhaṃ pracakrire
english: Seeing Sahasrākṣa stupefied by the sin of Brahmin-slaughter, they placed him at their head and performed the horse-sacrifice on behalf of the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tato 'śvamedhaḥ sumahān mahendrasya mahātmanaḥ vavṛdhe brahmahatyāyāḥ pāvanārthaṃ nareśvara
english: Then that great horse-sacrifice of the great-souled Mahendra grew and flourished for the purpose of purifying him from the sin of Brahmin-slaughter, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tato yajñasamāptau tu brahmahatyā mahātmanaḥ abhigamyābravīd vākyaṃ kva me sthānaṃ vidhāsyatha
english: Then, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, the Brahmin-slaughter [brahmahatyā] of the great-souled one approached [the gods] and said: "Where shall you assign me a dwelling place?"

sanskrit: te tām ūcus tato devās tuṣṭāḥ prītisamanvitāḥ caturdhā vibhajātmānam ātmanaiva durāsade
english: Then the gods, satisfied and filled with delight, said to her: "Divide yourself into four parts of your own accord, O formidable one."

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā brahmahatyā mahātmanām saṃnidhau sthānam anyatra varayām āsa durvasā
english: Having heard the words of the great-souled gods, Brahmin-slaughter, the dreadful one, sought to choose a different abode in their presence.

sanskrit: ekenāṃśena vatsyāmi pūrṇodāsu nadīṣu vai dvitīyena tu vṛkṣeṣu satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ
english: "With one portion I shall dwell in rivers swollen with water; with a second portion in trees — I tell you this as truth."

sanskrit: yo 'yam aṃśas tṛtīyo me strīṣu yauvanaśāliṣu trirātraṃ darpaparṇāsu vasiṣye darpaghātinī
english: "This third portion of mine shall dwell in women in the flush of youth, for the three nights [of their monthly season] when they are intoxicated with pride — I, the destroyer of pride."

sanskrit: hantāro brāhmaṇān ye tu prekṣāpūrvam adūṣakān tāṃś caturthena bhāgena saṃśrayiṣye surarṣabhāḥ
english: "Those who deliberately slay Brahmins that are blameless — with that fourth portion shall I take refuge in them, O bulls among gods."

sanskrit: pratyūcus tāṃ tato devā yathā vadasi durvase tathā bhavatu tat sarvaṃ sādhayasva yathepsitam
english: The gods then replied to her: "Let it all be exactly as you say, O terrible one; accomplish what you desire."

sanskrit: tataḥ prītyānvitā devāḥ sahasrākṣaṃ vavandire vijvaraḥ pūtapāpmā ca vāsavaḥ samapadyata
english: Then the gods, filled with joy, paid homage to Sahasrākṣa; and Vāsava became free from fever and purified of sin.

sanskrit: praśāntaṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ sahasrākṣe pratiṣṭhate yajñaṃ cādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ tadā śakro 'bhyapūjayat
english: And when Sahasrākṣa was reinstated, the entire world became calm; then Śakra duly honored that wondrous sacrifice.

sanskrit: īdṛśo hy aśvamedhasya prabhāvo raghunandana yajasva sumahābhāga hayamedhena pārthiva
english: "Such indeed is the power of the horse-sacrifice, O joy of the Raghu lineage; do you, O greatly blessed sovereign, perform the horse-sacrifice."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ prahasan rāghavo vacaḥ
english: Having heard those words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, the greatly resplendent Rāghava, skilled in speech, replied with a smile.

sanskrit: evam etan naraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa vṛtraghātam aśeṣeṇa vājimedhaphalaṃ ca yat
english: "It is exactly so, O best of men, just as you say, Lakṣmaṇa — [you have narrated] the full account of the slaying of Vṛtra and whatever is the fruit of the horse-sacrifice."

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purā saumya kardamasya prajāpateḥ putro bāhlīśvaraḥ śrīmān ilo nāma sudhārmikaḥ
english: "For it is heard, O gentle one, that in former times there was a son of Kardama Prajāpati — Ila by name, the lord of the Bāhlīkas, glorious and supremely righteous."

sanskrit: sa rājā pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ vaśe kṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ rājyaṃ caiva naravyāghra putravat paryapālayat
english: "That greatly renowned king, having brought the entire earth under his sway, governed his kingdom like a father cares for his son, O tiger among men."

sanskrit: suraiś ca paramodārair daiteyaiś ca mahāsuraiḥ nāgarākṣasagandharvair yakṣaiś ca sumahātmabhiḥ
english: "By the supremely noble gods, by the daityas and the great asuras, by the nāgas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and the great-souled yakṣas —"

sanskrit: pūjyate nityaśaḥ saumya bhayārtai raghunandana abibhyaṃś ca trayo lokāḥ saroṣasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "— he was constantly honored by them all, stricken with fear, O gentle one, O joy of the Raghu lineage; and the three worlds trembled before that great-souled one when he was wrathful."

sanskrit: sa rājā tādṛśo hy āsīd dharme vīrye ca niṣṭhitaḥ buddhyā ca paramodāro bāhlīkānāṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: "Such was that king — steadfast in righteousness and valor, supremely noble in intellect, the greatly renowned lord of the Bāhlīkas."

sanskrit: sa pracakre mahābāhur mṛgayāṃ rucire vane caitre manorame māsi sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: "That long-armed one set out on a hunt in a beautiful forest during the delightful month of Caitra, together with his retinue, army, and elephants."

sanskrit: prajaghne sa nṛpo 'raṇye mṛgāñ śatasahasraśaḥ hatvaiva tṛptir nābhūc ca rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "That king slew deer in the forest by the hundreds of thousands; yet even having slain so many, that great-souled king felt no satisfaction."

sanskrit: nānāmṛgāṇām ayutaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā yatra jāto mahāsenas taṃ deśam upacakrame
english: "While ten thousand beasts of various kinds were being slain by that great-souled one, he came upon the region where great Skanda [Mahāsena] was born."

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu devadeveśaḥ śailarājasutāṃ haraḥ ramayām āsa durdharṣaiḥ sarvair anucaraiḥ saha
english: "In that place, Hara — the lord of the lords of gods — was sporting with Pārvatī [the daughter of the mountain king] together with all his formidable attendants."

sanskrit: kṛtvā strībhūtam ātmānam umeśo gopatidhvajaḥ devyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ sa tasmin parvatanirjhare
english: "The lord of Umā, he whose banner bears the bull, having transformed himself into a woman, desiring to please the goddess, [dwelt] in that mountain cascade."

sanskrit: ye ca tatra vanoddeśe sattvāḥ puruṣavādinaḥ yac ca kiṃ cana tat sarvaṃ nārīsaṃjñaṃ babhūva ha
english: "And whatever creatures there were in that region of the forest that were called male, and whatever else existed there — all of it became feminine in nature."

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājā sa ilaḥ kardamātmajaḥ nighnan mṛgasahasrāṇi taṃ deśam upacakrame
english: "Meanwhile, the king Ila, son of Kardama, slaying thousands of deer, arrived at that very region."

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā strīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ savyālamṛgapakṣiṇam ātmānaṃ sānugaṃ caiva strībhūtaṃ raghunandana
english: "He saw that everything there — serpents, deer, and birds — had been made feminine, and that he himself along with his retinue had likewise become female, O joy of the Raghu lineage."

sanskrit: tasya duḥkhaṃ mahat tv āsīd dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ tathā gatam umāpateś ca tat karma jñātvā trāsam upāgamat
english: "He was seized with great grief on seeing himself reduced to such a state, and knowing it to be the act of Umāpati [Śiva], he was overcome with terror."

sanskrit: tato devaṃ mahātmānaṃ śitikaṇṭhaṃ kapardinam jagāma śaraṇaṃ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: "Then the king, together with his retinue, army, and elephants, took refuge with that great-souled god — the blue-throated one, Kapardī [Śiva with matted locks]."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya varadaḥ saha devyā mahāyaśāḥ prajāpatisutaṃ vākyam uvāca varadaḥ svayam
english: "Then the boon-granting one, greatly renowned, smiling and together with the goddess, himself spoke these words to the son of Prajāpati:"

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rājarṣe kārdameya mahābala puruṣatvam ṛte saumya varaṃ varaya suvrata
english: "'Arise, arise, O royal seer, O son of Kardama, O greatly powerful one! Choose a boon, O gentle one of good vows — any boon except manhood [itself].'"

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā śokārtāḥ pratyākhyāto mahātmanā na sa jagrāha strībhūto varam anyaṃ surottamāt
english: "Then that king, afflicted with grief, having been refused by the great-souled one, did not accept any other boon from that best of gods, while remaining in female form."

sanskrit: tataḥ śokena mahatā śailarājasutāṃ nṛpaḥ praṇipatya mahādevīṃ sarveṇaivāntarātmanā
english: "Then, with great grief, the king prostrated himself before Mahādevī — the daughter of the king of mountains — with his whole inner self."

sanskrit: īśe varāṇāṃ varade lokānām asi bhāmini amoghadarśane devi bhaje saumye namo 'stu te
english: "'You are the sovereign and bestower of boons upon the worlds, O beautiful one; O goddess of unerring vision, O gentle one, I adore you — homage be to you!'"

sanskrit: hṛdgataṃ tasya rājarṣer vijñāya harasaṃnidhau pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ devī rudrasya saṃmatā
english: "Knowing what was in the heart of that royal seer, the goddess — honored by Rudra — spoke these auspicious words in the presence of Hara:"

sanskrit: ardhasya devo varado varārdhasya tathā hy aham tasmād ardhaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ strīpuṃsor yāvad icchasi
english: "'The god grants boons of one half, and I likewise grant boons of the other half; therefore take the half boon [available from me] — alternating between womanhood and manhood for as long as you wish.'"

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ śrutvā devyā varam anuttamam saṃprahṛṣṭamanā bhūtvā rājā vākyam athābravīt
english: "Having heard that most wondrous and unsurpassed boon from the goddess, the king, his mind filled with great delight, then spoke:"

sanskrit: yadi devi prasannā me rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi māsaṃ strītvam upāsitvā māsaṃ syāṃ puruṣaḥ punaḥ
english: "'If you, O goddess — peerless in beauty on earth — are pleased with me, then [may I] having passed one month in womanhood, again become a man for one month.'"

sanskrit: īpsitaṃ tasya vijñāya devī surucirānanā pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyam evam etad bhaviṣyati
english: "Knowing his desire, the goddess of lovely countenance spoke these auspicious words: 'So shall it be.'"

sanskrit: rājan puruṣabhūtas tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na smariṣyasi strībhūtaś cāparaṃ māsaṃ na smariṣyasi pauruṣam
english: "'O king, when you are in the form of a man you shall not remember your female existence, and when you are in the form of a woman for the other month you shall not remember your manhood.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā puruṣo māmaṃ bhūtvātha kārdamiḥ trailokyasundarī nārī māsam ekam ilābhavat
english: "Thus that king, the son of Kardama, having been a man for one month, became for one month a woman beautiful as the three worlds — she became Ilā."
